Coulter Method for the detection of Physiological parameters
- Increase productivity with consistently reliable results.
- Flexible specially-formulated reagents, fully automated QC and calibration platforms provide consistently reliable results.

steps.title: Prepare safety and workspace
steps.instruction: Wear a lab coat and gloves, turn on the exhaust fan, ensure all required chemicals and reagents are available, clean all apparatus with chromic acid followed by distilled water, keep all glassware free of water droplets, handle cuvettes with tissue paper (no direct hand contact), and wipe cuvette exteriors with lint‑free cloth before use.

steps.title: Warm up the analyzer
steps.instruction: Turn on the Hitachi 7180 automatic analyzer and allow it to warm up for fifteen (15) minutes to achieve stable readings.

steps.title: Prepare samples and blank
steps.instruction: While the analyzer is warming, prepare each experimental sample in a 5 mL test tube and prepare a blank (control solution) using the same chemical solvent and the same volume as the samples, placed in an identical cuvette.

steps.title: Load sample and blank into cuvettes
steps.instruction: Transfer exactly 1 mL of each sample into a cuvette using a dedicated pipette for that sample (different pipettes for each to avoid cross‑contamination). Do the same for the blank.

steps.title: Clean cuvette exterior
steps.instruction: Wipe the outside of each cuvette with a lint‑free cloth to remove water droplets and dust before loading it into the analyzer.

steps.title: Select analysis wavelength
steps.instruction: Choose a single monochromatic wavelength that corresponds to the absorption maximum of the target chemical (as specified by the spectrophotometer) and set this wavelength on the analyzer.

steps.title: Calibrate analyzer with blank
steps.instruction: Place the blank cuvette into the holder, close the lid, observe the analog needle move, record the reading, then turn the adjustment knob until the needle reads zero. Leave the blank in place while zeroing.

steps.title: Verify calibration stability
steps.instruction: Remove the blank; the needle should remain at zero. Re‑insert the blank to confirm the reading does not change, ensuring the calibration is stable for the session (one blank per session).

steps.title: Measure sample absorbance
steps.instruction: Remove the blank, insert the sample cuvette upright into the designated groove, wait approximately ten (10) seconds until the needle (or digital display) stabilizes, then record the % transmittance and/or absorbance value.

steps.title: Repeat measurements at multiple wavelengths
steps.instruction: Change the wavelength in 25 nm increments across the desired spectral range and repeat the absorbance measurement for each sample at each wavelength.

steps.title: Calculate transmittance and absorbance
steps.instruction: Compute transmittance (T) as T = I/I₀, where I is the intensity from the sample and I₀ is the intensity from the blank. Then calculate absorbance (A) using A = ‑log₁₀(T).

steps.title: Plot absorbance spectrum
steps.instruction: Plot absorbance (y‑axis) versus wavelength (x‑axis) for each sample, marking the maximum absorbance at each wavelength to generate the absorbance spectrum.

steps.title: Compare spectrum to reference data
steps.instruction: Compare the obtained absorbance spectrum to known spectra of reference compounds; identify peaks that match known wavelengths to determine the composition of the sample and detect any unexpected contaminants.
